items.title: How Far Can GE Stock Move When The Work Is Already Booked?
items.summary: GE Aerospace (GE) has more engine work booked than it can currently perform, and that visibility is much of why people own the shares. The option chain does not treat the stock as settled. At about $307, contracts running twelve months out carry a band from near $216.93 to near $434.6, with roughly a two-in-three chance the stock finishes inside it.

items.title: SpaceX Regains $150 IPO Open Price as Defense Dept. Confirms Space-Based Weapons
items.summary: The Pentagon just confirmed on-orbit space weapons, and SpaceX sits at the center of a multibillion-dollar architecture that transforms that announcement into hard contracts. Here is what the move means for the stock and the sector names getting pulled along with it.

items.title: 5 Elite Dividend Stocks Backed by America’s Massive Defense Budget
items.summary: Defense contractors sell to a customer whose budget is written into law years in advance, and that single fact changes everything about how their dividends behave. Five names are quietly turning trillion-dollar Pentagon commitments into income streams most investors overlook.

items.title: What Are You Actually Buying In RKLB Stock?
items.summary: Rocket Lab (RKLB) stock has traded between $39.48 and $150.23 over the past 52 weeks. It now sits about 58% below its 52-week high, and anyone who bought twelve months ago is still up about 19%. None of that tells you what you would be buying today. Rocket Lab sells two quite different things, and the one its name points at is the smaller of them.

items.title: Space Weapons: How Boeing, SpaceX, and Others Stand to Gain
items.summary: On Monday, the U.S. Space Force confirmed the existence of space-based weapons, though what exactly is in space is classified.  The news represents a milestone in military technology.  Space is the new strategic high ground.

items.title: Why Is Boeing Stock Falling While Revenue Soars Past Peers?
items.summary: Boeing (BA) grew revenue faster over the past twelve months than any of its aerospace and defense peers, GE Aerospace included, and its stock still fell. It is also the only one in that group running an operating loss. The growth has come with rising airplane deliveries, and the market is waiting to see whether those airplanes earn a margin.
